evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.text: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -- corroborating uses of the {{rd|melee|ranged}} template, used to pin argument order from the cache alone
text: Iceborn Gauntlet / Spellblade: 'slowed by {{rd|25%|{{ap|25*0.5}}%}}'  (2nd arg literally written as 25*0.5)
Hullbreaker / Skipper: '{{rd|120%|{{ap|120*0.7}}%}} base AD'      (2nd arg literally written as 120*0.7)
Doran's Shield / Enduring Focus: '{{rd|0 to 5 for 11|0 to 3.75 for 11|...}}' (2nd arg = 75% of 1st)
Ravenous Hydra / Tiamat / Stridebreaker / Profane Hydra / Cleave: '{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}'
Blade of the Ruined King / Mist's Edge: '{{rd|9%|6%}} of the target's current health'
sources_quoted.conclusion: The second argument of {{rd|A|B}} is always the REDUCED (ranged) value, written in several items as an explicit fraction of the first. Therefore {{rd|8%|5%}} = 8% for a MELEE Bloodsong holder, 5% for a RANGED holder.

sources_quoted.text: f(S) = the coupled participant-timeline score: deterministic total damage dealt by the main participant before its own death, summed over the fight window, with an infinitesimal effective-health tiebreak.

m(R) = 100/(100+R); and: 'Black Cleaver average stacks: the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch). ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C'

independent_computation.limitation_stated_up_front: The exported evidence tree (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md) does NOT contain the scenario input tuple for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' -- no champions, levels, ranks, item lists, fight window, or target resistances. data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json has no cleaver/Bloodsong/roster entry, and no file under data/ mentions the scenario. The absolute total therefore cannot be recomputed from first principles inside the permitted evidence tree. What CAN be computed independently is (a) the correct value of the wiki-pinned parameter the leaf depends on, and (b) which of the two candidate values reproduces both reported numbers exactly under a physically admissible decomposition.

step_1_parameter_from_wiki.claim: Bloodsong's Expose Weakness grants the target +8% damage taken from all sources for a melee holder, +5% for a ranged holder.
step_1_parameter_from_wiki.derivation: S1 gives the raw value as {{rd|8%|5%}}. S3 pins the template's argument order from the cache itself: in Iceborn Gauntlet the second argument is spelled '25*0.5' and in Hullbreaker '120*0.7' -- i.e. the second slot is always the ranged-reduced value, never the melee value. Cross-checked against three more items whose melee/ranged split is well known (Ravenous Hydra 40%/20%, Titanic Hydra 1%/0.5%, Blade of the Ruined King 9%/6%). Conclusion: melee = 8%.
step_1_parameter_from_wiki.scenario_side: The scenario pairs Black Cleaver (S2: an armor-shred fighter item -- 40 AD / 400 HP / 20 AH, shred triggered by dealing physical damage) with Bloodsong. Black Cleaver's Carve applies its full 6%-per-stack shred on physical damage; the Bloodsong line is the melee-support upgrade of Bounty of Worlds. A melee holder is the reading the fixture name supports, so 8% is the applicable branch.

step_2_decomposition_of_the_reported_del.model: Let U = damage dealt while Expose Weakness is NOT up (pre-first-Spellblade), and X = pre-amp damage dealt while it IS up. Then total = U + (1+a)*X for amp a.
step_2_decomposition_of_the_reported_del.plausibility: Under this decomposition 3024.0 / 3310.1 = 91.4% of the focus damage lands under Expose Weakness. With a 4 s debuff duration and a 1.5 s re-application cooldown, uptime after the first Spellblade proc is effectively continuous, so ~91% uptime corresponds to the debuff going live roughly one second into the fight window. That is the expected shape.
step_2_decomposition_of_the_reported_del.conclusion: The old value is exactly the 5% (RANGED) branch of {{rd|8%|5%}}; the new value is exactly the 8% (MELEE) branch. Nothing else about the fight moved -- U and X are identical between the two.

step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: Amp newly added where it was previously absent (0% -> 8%).
step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.requires: X = 84.0/0.08 = 1050.0, i.e. only 34.3% of the focus damage under the debuff.
step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: A 4 s debuff on a 1.5 s cooldown cannot have ~34% uptime in a sustained fight; and the resulting U = 2176.1 of un-amplified damage is inconsistent with a fixture built specifically to exercise Expose Weakness.

step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: Amp newly added at the ranged value (0% -> 5%).
step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: Same uptime objection, weaker; and it would leave the leaf on the wrong (ranged) branch, so it cannot be the correct value even if it were the mechanism.

step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: Black Cleaver average-stacks model replaced by the Cesaro mean recommended in math-foundations Section 2.3 (constant 0.8*C = 4 stacks = 24% shred -> C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h stacks = 30% - 60%/h shred).
step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.requires: Solving (100 + A*(1-0.24)) / (100 + A*(1-r_new)) = 3310.1/3226.1 for the target's pre-shred armor A, assuming the ENTIRE leaf is armor-mitigated physical damage (the most generous case): h=12 -> no solution (the model moves the wrong way, since 5-10/h < 4 for h < 10 and the swing is too small at h=12); h=15 -> A = 3556 (absurd); h=20 -> A = 237; h=30 -> A = 122; h=60 -> A = 83.
step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: Only h >= ~20 hits combined with a very high armor target admits a solution, and every non-physical or true-damage component in the leaf pushes the required armor higher still. More decisively, this mechanism cannot produce the exact pair (3226.1, 3310.1) from a round decomposition the way the 5%/8% branch swap does, and it predicts BOTH signs of change across the corpus (damage falls for h < 10), whereas this leaf's delta is a clean +84.0 = 0.03 * 2800.0.

step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: Uniform rescale of the whole leaf by 1.08/1.05.
step_3_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: 3226.1 * 1.08/1.05 = 3318.3, not 3310.1. Also 33101/32261 has gcd 1, so the change is not a uniform multiplicative scale -- it is an additive delta on a proper subset, exactly as the U + (1+a)X decomposition says.

independent_computation.residual_uncertainty: Because the scenario tuple is outside the permitted evidence tree, I verified the parameter and the exact reproduction of both reported numbers, not the absolute total. If the 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' Bloodsong holder were RANGED, the correct branch would be 5% and the old value would stand; nothing in data/ names the holder, but the fixture's own name (Black Cleaver, a melee-fighter shred item, paired with the melee-support Bloodsong upgrade) and the exactness of the 8% reconstruction both point melee.

verdict_rationale: The League Wiki cache pins Expose Weakness at 8% increased damage taken for a melee holder ({{rd|8%|5%}}, argument order pinned from the cache itself by S3). The new golden value 3310.1 is reproduced exactly by 286.1 + 1.08 * 2800.0; the old value 3226.1 is reproduced exactly by 286.1 + 1.05 * 2800.0 -- i.e. the old number was computed on the ranged branch of the same template. The new value is the wiki-correct one.
